classification.difficultyReason: Select a minimum spanning tree connecting six ponds and the entrance, then convert its total length into a paving cost.

content.prompt:
A Japanese garden is being built, with paths connecting ponds.

The cost to pave the paths is $\$120$ per metre. What is the least cost of the paths?

spec.description: Seven labelled vertices, including the entrance junction. The twelve undirected paths and their weights are preserved. A–B, A–Entrance and E–F are curved. Pond illustrations are represented by clear vertex markers under house style.
spec.mathematics: Lengths in metres: AB=45, AC=50, A–Entrance=60, BC=45, BD=50, CD=45, CE=45, C–Entrance=40, DE=60, DF=50, EF=40, E–Entrance=25.
spec.answerVisibility: All network edges, weights and labels are permanent givens; no selected spanning tree or answer is shown.

answer.worked:
A minimum spanning tree uses Pond A–Pond B, Pond B–Pond C, Pond C–Pond D, Pond C–Entrance, Entrance–Pond E and Pond E–Pond F. These six paths connect all seven sites without a cycle.

$\begin{aligned}\text{Total length}&=45+45+45+40+25+40\\&=240\text{ m}\\\text{Least cost}&=240\times120\\&=\$28\,800\end{aligned}$

spec.description: The minimum spanning tree retains the source vertex arrangement and shows only the six selected paths, with all site labels and selected weights.
spec.mathematics: Selected edges AB, BC, CD, C–Entrance, Entrance–E and EF have total length 240 metres.
